prompt.context: The client is the North American CEO of a global personal and home care products company. He has hired Capgemini Consulting to turn around the North American business from loss to profitability within two years. We've scheduled the final presentation with the board this afternoon, but the project team is stranded at an airport unable to make the presentation. You are asked to step in and make the presentation instead.
prompt.question: How would you structure the analysis needed to turn around the North American business from loss to profitability within two years?

clarifying_info.q: What are the main revenue streams?
What are the main cost drivers?
What other internal considerations are relevant?
clarifying_info.a: Supply chain, channel strategy, financial situation, org structure, and core competencies.
The key competitors cater to different customer segments; intensity of rivalry varies by segment.

clarifying_info.q: Through what retail channels are products sold?
clarifying_info.a: Products are sold through various retail channels; their relative power positions are a key consideration.

clarifying_info.q: What are the different consumer segments?
clarifying_info.a: Consumer segments differ by demographics; understanding their relative sizes and the client's main consumers is important.

exhibits.title: 2012-2017 Growth in Personal Care Consumption by Age Group
exhibits.shows: A chart showing growth rates in personal care consumption across age groups and genders in Mexico, USA, and Canada for the period 2012-2017.
exhibits.data: Growth figures segmented by age group (e.g., 55+, Baby Boomers born 1945-1965, Generation X born 1965-1985, Echo Boomers born 1985-1995) and by male/female across three North American regions.

exhibits.title: Ranking Major Household Spending Categories by Share of Wallet and Perception of Need
exhibits.shows: A scatter plot mapping major spending categories on two axes: perception of need (Necessity to Luxury) on the horizontal axis and share of wallet (Low to High) on the vertical axis.
exhibits.data: Categories plotted include Taxes, Housing, Food, Insurance/Pension, Clothing, Household Operations, Personal Care (1.7% share of wallet), Household Products (4.5% share of wallet), Recreation, Education, Health Care, Donations/Contributions, Tobacco/Alcohol, and Household Furnishings & Equipment.

exhibits.title: Product-Channel Strategy Map
exhibits.shows: A matrix mapping competitors by their product category breadth against their channel strategy (dedicated vs. diverse).
exhibits.data: Competitors are positioned on axes reflecting product diversity and channel strategy; examples include Estee Lauder (diverse channels: prestigious retail, company-run salons, brand websites) and The Body Shop (dedicated channel: 2,000+ stores worldwide plus web channel).

framework: Internal Analysis: Revenue streams (existing & new products), cost drivers (R&D, manufacturing, operations), supply chain, channel strategy, financial situation, org structure, core competencies
Industry Analysis: Competitor landscape (segments served, rivalry intensity, consolidation/price war trends), retail channel power positions
Customer Analysis: Consumer segments (size, saturation, the client's core consumers), trends (are tastes shifting toward or away from client products)

questions.prompt: Review Exhibits 1, 2, and 3. What are your key observations and what analysis would you take to the CEO?
questions.guidance: Exhibit 1 — Women dominate personal care consumption across all three regions; Female Baby Boomers (born 1945-1965) are the primary growth driver (Mexico +8.63%, USA +5.31%, Canada +5.98%) due to large numbers and high spending power from wealth accumulation and inheritance; male 55+ is a small but relatively faster-growing segment; Gen X is underrepresented (except Mexico due to higher population growth 1965-85); Echo Boomers will matter post-2010 but are short-term watch items. Exhibit 2 — Share of wallet correlates directly with perception of necessity; Personal Care sits at 1.7% and Household Products at 4.5% of wallet; moving products up the necessity axis is key to capturing larger wallet share. Exhibit 3 — Companies with dedicated channel strategies favor direct selling for maximum consumer interaction; a trend toward channel diversification exists because different products require distinct channels; the client's large product portfolio suggests it should pursue a diverse distribution strategy rather than a single dedicated channel.

questions.prompt: Beyond the three exhibits, what other considerations should you inform the CEO need further analysis?
questions.guidance: In-house manufacturing vs. outsource: pros/cons, key constraints and criteria, competitor benchmarks. Customer: impact of country-of-origin on consumer perception and brand/marketing strategy. Location/distribution network: does the current design support future growth given all costs, and what distance span optimizes service vs. cost? Decision-making process: current state vs. ideal Make/Buy decision process, accountability and ownership. Scalability: how distribution centers scale with growth projections, number of DCs needed, optimal range per DC.

brainstorming.prompt: What considerations should the CEO be informed need further analysis beyond the three charts?

categories.name: Distribution Network
ideas: Does current network support future growth?
Optimal distance span to balance service and cost

categories.name: Decision-Making Process
ideas: Current state of Make/Buy decision process
Accountability and ownership for Make/Buy decisions

categories.name: Scalability
ideas: How DCs scale with growth projections
How many DCs will be required

recommendation: Focus on women as the primary target segment (lion's share of consumption), while monitoring growth in the 55+ male group; account for geographic differences within North America.
Develop deep knowledge of customer needs, perception, and spending patterns to capture increased share of wallet — critical for long-term sustainable growth.
Shift to a more diverse distribution channel strategy given the client's large number of product categories; current channel positioning is misaligned.
risks: Market growth may slow or enter decline, making projections unreliable.
Threat of substitute products and changing consumer trends could reduce the perceived necessity of the client's products.
next_steps: Invest in customer research to better understand needs by segment and geography.
Increase marketing spend to reposition products higher on the necessity axis.
Conduct thorough cost-benefit analysis of options for diversifying distribution channels.
